name: Cervicoplasty / Cervical contouring
lead: Cervicoplasty is a plastic-surgery term for contouring the neck by working on skin, fat and sometimes muscle. In aesthetic practice it is part of neck rejuvenation, and it also appears in reconstruction after burn contractures [1][9]. Looksmaxxing communities group it among hardmaxxing procedures aimed at a cleaner neck and jaw transition.

The literature contains surgeon-described techniques, anatomical studies and case series. A 1997 report described a non-excisional anterior approach through a submental incision without removing skin, for patients with good skin contraction [2]. Anatomical research has mapped fat compartments of the neck in cadavers [3]. No randomized trials of aesthetic cervicoplasty were found.

paras: A nonexcisional anterior technique uses a 3 to 4 cm incision behind the submental crease, with a thick subcutaneous flap and endoscope-assisted fat removal, in patients whose skin can redrape [2]. A comprehensive approach to neck rejuvenation emphasises analysis of the lower face and deep structures, and notes bone resorption as a component of aging [4]. A 2021 review addressed optimizing outcomes in neck lift surgery [6]. Other papers examine specific fat compartments, including the subplatysmal supramylohyoid fat [8], and lifting methods such as the MACS-lift [10].

Cervicoplasty has been combined with thin free flaps, such as anterolateral thigh [1] and thoracodorsal artery perforator flaps [9], to reconstruct postburn neck contractures. These are medical reconstruction series, not cosmetic outcomes.

Studies are small surgical series and anatomical work: seven patients with free anterolateral thigh flap and cervicoplasty [1], a cadaver study of ten heads [3], and technique papers [2][4][10]. One registered trial, NCT05515016, tested a fatty flap from the double chin for chin enhancement in ten participants; the registry lists it as completed [11].

timeline.event: Cadaver study defines fat compartments of the neck [3].

card.summary: Surgical contouring of neck skin, fat and muscle; documented in surgical series, with little controlled evidence.
card.note: Evidence is surgeon technique papers and small series; the term also covers burn reconstruction.

quick.overview:
Cervicoplasty means reshaping the neck surgically, by managing skin, fat and sometimes muscle. It is used in aesthetic neck lifts and in reconstruction after burns.

The literature is technique descriptions, cadaver work and small series.
quick.mechanism: Surgeons remove or redistribute fat, tighten tissue and may redrape or excise skin, sometimes through a small incision under the chin.
quick.risks: Operative risks apply, and outcomes depend on skin quality as described in technique papers. No randomized trial data were found.
